Hi Soojin — thanks for the clear note. Short answers below plus a sample MT103 trace attached.

1) Path behavior: For EUR->UK (our correspondent chain), the most common outcome is that the intermediary (correspondent) deducts a single fee which appears on the MT103 as an "intermediary charge". In a minority of cases the respondent bank (beneficiary's bank) will also add a separate processing fee; when that happens you'll often see both an intermediary and a beneficiary charge listed. So default = net-of-single-intermediary fee, but not guaranteed.

2) OUR vs BEN: We can accept instructions with "OUR" to push fees onto the sender; however, even with OUR, some bridge/respondent banks may still deduct micro-fees for their routing. Practically speaking, for high-confidence full-credit to beneficiary we recommend: use OUR + add a conservative gross-up of 0.35%-0.75% depending on corridor and amount (lower bound for large transfers). For an EUR 100k payment, 0.35% tends to be sufficient; for smaller amounts or more opaque corridors use 0.75%.

3) VAT reclaim: The MT103 shows the amounts and fee descriptions; the attached mt103-sample.txt demonstrates how deductions appear and which BIC recorded the deduction. For VAT reclaim, you generally need an invoice from the party that charged the VATable service (e.g., intermediary bank invoice). We can request an intermediary invoice in pro forma if required, but many banks do not issue VAT-style invoices for correspondent fees — reclaimability depends on local VAT rules and whether the service is considered taxable.

Actionable next steps for you:
- Use the attached wire_template.xlsx: set Field 56A (Intermediary) to BIC XXXXXX, Field 57A (Account with institution) to the beneficiary's correspondent as we indicated.
- Put charge instruction = OUR and put a gross-up % in the <amount gross-up> field — we recommend 0.5% as a midpoint for this corridor.
- If GlobalRetailer needs documentary evidence for VAT reclaim, we can open a ticket to request a trace invoice from the correspondent bank. That can take 5-10 business days.

Attaching: mt103-sample.txt (anonymized)

Regards,
Marco Rossi
GlobalPay Operations
